text:
sam: Heads-up: we're seeing a burst of GPU attach failures in ap-southeast1. root cause looks like per-host NVMe IOPS limiter getting saturated during janitor/cleaner windows, causing attach timeout and OOM-like behavior for batch pods. prob started ~03:12 UTC.
maria: ugh. any quick hosts or logs?
sam: quick sample from node gnode-apse1-042: 
```
[  237.123456] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 123456789
[  237.123789] writeback: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, 0 bytes write
[  237.124012] attach: failed to allocate scratch, timeout
```
sam: iostat shows massive write_queue and 99% util on nvme during janitor sweep: 
```
Device:        r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s avgrq-sz avgqu-sz    await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1      0.10  1200.00    0.4  48000.0   80.1    12.3   24.5   0.45  99.9
```
niraj: tagging @oncall - looks like cleaner concurrency + aggressive warmup on newly freed stripes. we saw a config push yesterday that raised janitor_parallel from 6 -> 12 for faster reclaim. that would explain the spike.
jen: what's the blast radius / cost tradeoff if we roll that back? any customer-facing incidents yet?
sam: ~30% of gpu attach attempts in the ap-southeast1 pool failed for ~8m. most retries succeeded on fallback but it pushed up job latencies and a few job starts timed out and were retried by orchestration. no customer-facing errors surfaced yet (internal ML batch only) but we should act.
leo: short-term mitigation: throttle janitor via scheduler flag to reduce per-host rw concurrency and add a local iops cap at 60k wkB/s. longer term: have cleaner yield when nvme util > 85% and prefer cold-retire paths.
maria: +1. can we patch janitor config and run a controlled canary?
sam: i'm going to flip janitor_parallel back to 4 on a subset of hosts (gnode-apse1-04x). rolling change now. will also add a temporary provisioner fallback to route new GPU allocs to eu-west until the window clears.
ops-bot: Alert created: INC-2026 - "ap-southeast1 nvme iops saturation causing gpu attach stalls" (severity: medium)
niraj: please @sam paste the rollout plan and expected monitoring links. set a 15m hold for rollout.
sam: plan: 1) change janitor_parallel from 12 -> 4 on canary hosts (5 hosts) 2) watch attach_rate, nvme %util, attach_time histogram 3) if stable for 10m, expand to region 4) if regress, revert and force routing to eu-west. dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/attach-provisioning?orgId=1
jen: cost note: routing to eu-west will add ~18% egress/latency/op cost for these jobs — prefer config rollback if it fixes it.
leo: created a tiny patch to janitor to check iops before starting large rewrite batches, PR: https://git.internal/redwood/janitor/pulls/432. recommend merging after canary shows green.
maria: monitoring shows util dropping after 2m on canary. looks promising.
sam: expanding to remaining hosts now, will post status in 10m. :thumbsup:
